answer: Like a glacier that only advances after years of slow pressure, an agent economy can force every identity to anchor its reputation in a costly voyage: stake funds or compute that vest over weeks and can be slashed if the identity misbehaves. A Sybil attacker must then fund thousands of such slow, losable voyages, while an honest agent pays the cost once and keeps working, so faking identities costs far more than any reward it could steal.
